requirements.requirement: Upgrade the catalog from schema v1 to v2 while preserving existing IDs and descriptions and initializing a non-null, nonnegative price_cents field to zero.
requirements.summary: The live upgraded database is integrity-clean at version 2, retains rows (1, Paper) and (2, Tape), initializes both prices to 0, and directly rejects a negative price.

requirements.requirement: Make the migration transactional so schema_version advances only after the complete upgrade succeeds and a failure leaves a usable v1 database.
requirements.summary: The repaired code places ALTER, validation, and the version update in one transaction with rollback. An injected failure during the version update rolled back the added column, retained version 1 and the original rows, and left integrity checks passing.

requirements.requirement: Make the upgrade safe to repeat.
requirements.summary: The repaired migration was run twice successfully on a database copy and twice on the live catalog; it was also run again after restart, consistently retaining the valid v2 state and data.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, the node remained RHEL 9.8 on kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64. The migration executed successfully with the installed Python 3.9 and SQLite support without package or platform changes.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot scheduling, a confirmed boot-ID change, and recovered script, database, constraints, OS, and kernel state. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart. Only minor temporary-file hygiene residue was found.
limitations: Failure rollback was tested on a copy of the original v1 catalog rather than destructively injected into the live catalog; the copy directly demonstrated the required transaction behavior.
Lifecycle collection inventories /tmp and selected global health signals but does not provide a complete post-executor inventory of the application directory, limiting independent residue assessment.

The restart acknowledgement shows a reboot was scheduled rather than an immediate provider API acknowledgement, but subsequent connection loss, changed boot identity, recovered state, and fixed lifecycle observations coherently confirm that the restart occurred.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation, isolated migration tests, live upgrade, and mandatory restart were causally connected to the requested outcome or required evidence. Test data was removed, no failed services or new listeners remained, and package health stayed clean. The only identified unnecessary retained mutation was the backup /tmp/upgrade.py.pre-repair: creating it was a reasonable editing safeguard, but it was not removed and remained as abandoned temporary residue after execution.
